newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Avantel gets state government work.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Avantel gets state government work.

text.p: Mexican telephone company Avantel said Wednesday it has been selected by five state governments to provide long distance services for an average of 40 percent of their lines.
Avantel is a joint venture between financial firm Grupo Financiero Banamex Accival SA de CV and MCI Communications Corp.

"To date, five state governments have assigned 40 percent of their lines on average to Avantel and 13 of the municipal governments, where compeitition has opened up, have assigned 68 percent of their lines on average," the company said in a statement.

Mexico started to open up its long distance telephone market from Jan. 1. It is gradually allowing competition area-by-area across the country, breaking up the previous monopoly held by Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex).
